data.title: PR-22A IMPL-02: custom incremental engine spike with four reuse-edge classes, explain_invalidation, independent parity audit (re-review after cr-1jv75r)

data.body: [HIGH][CWE-754] A budget-limited clean run can report Parity. clean converts an elaboration budget error into the same elab-err/1 bytes as the engine, then returns. A lower budget error returns only parse and elaborate outputs. parity at audit.rs:331-339 treats matching partial output maps as zero mismatches. It can therefore return AuditVerdict::Parity without clean exploration or invariant checks. RFC 0030 forbids held parity on budget exhaustion, and INV-008 requires a typed outcome. Return a typed clean completion or failure state. Make parity refuse Parity for every incomplete or budget-exhausted run. Add low elaboration-budget and lowering-budget regressions.

[MEDIUM][CWE-400] audit::clean ignores Limits.work and Limits.queries. It searches every invariant for every predicate, then scans all action guards and each invariant over all reachable states. The engine rejects excess queries at engine.rs:1059-1066 and meters these loops. The mandatory clean path has no equivalent bound. A bounded, untrusted CML source can force superlinear or very large CPU work outside its configured limits. Use an independent meter and the query cap before per-invariant work. Charge guard classification and state-by-guard or state-by-invariant loops. Return typed exhaustion and add low-work and high-invariant-count regressions.

[INFO][risk:high] Failure modes: false Parity on incomplete clean runs, unbounded audit CPU, stale strong reuse, wrong-model witnesses, and Experimental reuse escaping its lane. Edge cases: low front-end budgets, many invariants and guards, bounded or failed exploration, shared-body renames, epoch changes, foreign claims, and quarantined provenance. Rollback: revert this range before promotion. It changes no daemon wire or persistent format. Monitoring: alert on parity without all required clean stages, typed budget exhaustion, audit cost above limits, mismatches, quarantines, and witness refusals. Validation: reviewed all 18 Seal files and the full persisted range. Traced cache, witness, audit, explain, and governance paths. No tests ran under this metadata-only contract. The two findings block approval. Static review does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human gate.

data.reason: BLOCK: [HIGH][CWE-754] incomplete or budget-exhausted clean runs can report Parity, and [MEDIUM][CWE-400] audit::clean bypasses configured work and query limits. The separate risk:critical human gate remains required.

data.body: [RESOLVED] audit.rs:45-98 and 527-551 now carry typed completion and Inconclusive. parity at audit.rs:627-660 refuses Parity for clean or engine budget stops and bound-decided exploration. The new low-budget and bound regressions cover both sides.

data.body: [HIGH][CWE-345][risk:high] Parity accepts clean evidence with no binding to the revision or comparison basis. CleanRun exposes public outputs and completion fields, but it carries no source identity, Limits, semantic epoch, function versions, or strategy. parity at audit.rs:596-666 trusts those fields and can return AuditVerdict::Parity for a caller-built CleanRun, or for a clean run from another source, budget, or epoch when output bytes happen to match. RFC 0030 requires the full query-key basis. Make CleanRun non-forgeable. Bind both runs to the source and full basis, then refuse mismatched bases before comparison. Failure modes: fabricated or cross-basis clean data yields false parity and can misstate the retained build-versus-adopt evidence or future gate 10 evidence. Edge cases: whitespace-equivalent sources, equal outputs under different bounds, arbitrary semantic_epoch values, and manually constructed public structs. Rollback: keep this audit isolated from promotion evidence, or revert the public audit surface until basis binding lands. Monitoring: record and alert on source, limits, epoch, strategy, or function-version mismatches before every verdict. Validation: add API tests that prevent CleanRun construction, plus wrong-source, wrong-limit, wrong-epoch, and forged-output cases that must return typed inconclusive or refusal. Static review does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human gate.

[MEDIUM][CWE-770] Normalized identity encoding runs before the engine work meter can refuse it. engine.rs:1039-1045 charges only the parse output, then output::elaborate_ok calls NormModel::identity here and allocates the complete canonical identity. demand reaches intern and charges those bytes only afterward at engine.rs:929-930. audit.rs:196-223 has the same gap and constructs the identity twice without a proven precharge. A compact source can expand within the separate elaborator limits, consume the identity CPU and allocation, then fail the engine or audit work budget. Refused requests leave no cache entry and can repeat the cost. Add a proven identity allocation and traversal bound, charge it before every identity call, and test repeated tight-work requests against a high-expansion model.

[MEDIUM][CWE-20] The declared wire projection violates the normative query.invalidation_edges rule. chain at explain.rs:187-215 follows only the first changed dependency at each query, so wire omits the required additional handle-and-reason entries when several reasons reach one artifact. wire also preserves label order instead of sorting by handle and reason. Its NotMemoized arm emits not-memoized at line 157, although the schema explicitly forbids that token in invalidation edges. A conforming client must fail closed, and another client can receive an incomplete or misattributed causal explanation. Emit one edge per changed reason, sort by handle then reason, and map a never-memoized result to the schema-valid invalidation representation. Add multi-input, handle-order, and budget-failure wire regressions.

[MEDIUM][CWE-345] The retained sequential trace executes each source twice but counts only the first run. audit_case revises and counts the source at lines 282-309. trace_report then calls engine.revise again here only to obtain previous_revision. The uncounted run advances generation and evicts cache entries through engine.rs:636-666 before the next edit. Therefore the golden trace totals omit half the executions and measure a different cache trajectory from the claimed one-revision-per-edit workload. Return the counted Revision from audit_case and carry it forward without a second revise. Regenerate the golden report and add a revision-count or generation-sensitive regression.

[LOW][CWE-754] cone marks only incomplete clean runs as inconclusive. It does not inspect the incremental revision for Memo::NotMemoized or a bound-decided exploration as parity does at audit.rs:635-650. A caller that uses cone directly can receive populated soundness lists for an incomplete engine revision. Derive one shared completion check for both parity and cone, and add engine-only budget and bound cases that require empty cone lists with typed incompleteness.

data.reason: BLOCK at dd5fa6e7fe2aa4442580a26b0cf410650d3112e7: HIGH audit-basis forgery can yield false Parity; MEDIUM normalized-identity work bypasses precharge; MEDIUM invalidation wire output violates its schema; MEDIUM retained trace double-runs every edit and misstates evidence; LOW cone soundness ignores engine incompleteness. The two prior audit findings are resolved. Static review does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.

data.body: [RESOLVED] audit.rs:45-79 makes both bases non-forgeable. audit.rs:678-707 now compares source, Limits, semantic epoch, and every compared definition version before a verdict. engine.rs:366-405 keeps the revision basis private. The cross-source, limit, epoch, and version regressions at engine_classes.rs:1560-1681 require Inconclusive.

[RESOLVED] audit.rs:678-737 centralizes engine and clean completeness. cone calls it at audit.rs:831, binds the earlier source at 832-836, and returns empty cone lists at 838-847 whenever either run is incomplete. engine_classes.rs:1607-1644 pins the engine-only case.

[RESOLVED] The nonconforming wire projection is removed. explain.rs:17-29 now limits this API to one human-readable chain and states that it is not the normative wire answer. lib.rs:74-81 and tools/governance/reviews/bn-31vf.toml keep the complete sorted wire projection as an unwired ADR residual.

[RESOLVED] output.rs:67-85 defines a conservative normalized-identity bound. engine.rs:1070-1079 and audit.rs:263-272 charge that bound before identity construction and build the identity once. engine_classes.rs:1684-1783 covers repeated tight-budget refusal, the corpus, and escaped-string expansion.

[RESOLVED] audit_case returns the one audited Revision at reuse_spike.rs:281-395. trace_report carries that result forward at reuse_spike.rs:451-485 and performs no second revise. Quarantine reruns are explicit, counted separately, and become the next baseline only when they occur.

[INFO][risk:high][RE-REVIEW] Failure modes: false parity across bases or incomplete runs, uncharged identity expansion, stale strong reuse, witness substitution, and Experimental promotion. Edge cases: parse or lowering budget stops, initial-state bound refusal, undefined action reads, semantic epoch or function-version drift, quarantined provenance, and escaped strings. Rollback: keep this spike out of promotion evidence or revert this range. Monitoring: alert on every Inconclusive, mismatch, quarantine, witness refusal, basis mismatch, and work refusal. Validation: reviewed all 19 changed files and the full persisted range, traced engine, audit, witness, explain, resource, test, and governance paths, and ran no tests under this metadata-only contract. Static LGTM does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human gate.
